established_findings.statement: LLM-based approaches for network configuration and repair show promise but frequently produce incorrect fixes, regressions, or other failure modes when evaluated at scale or in closed-loop execution.
limitations: Many benchmarked scenarios are synthetic or emulated rather than large-scale production deployments (see W7157506260, W7204209332).
Model and tool diversity in published evaluations is limited, so measured failure rates may vary with other models or integrations.

established_findings.statement: Iterative generate→validate→repair workflows that integrate formal verification or executable emulation materially improve the ability to detect and prevent semantic/network-level errors in LLM-produced configurations or fixes.
limitations: Integration complexity and performance cost of verification/digital-twin steps vary by tool and topology (reported studies focus on representative scenarios rather than exhaustive production heterogeneity).
Reported improvements derive from controlled experiments; operational rollouts may introduce additional telemetry/state-consistency challenges.

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented agent architectures and bounded-autonomy guardrails (e.g., veto layers, canary deployments, secure tool registries, runtime validation) are repeatedly proposed and evaluated as practical safety measures for agentic NetOps.
limitations: Empirical validation of these architectures in long-running production settings is limited; many evaluations are conceptual, prototype, or testbed-based.
Different guardrail designs trade off autonomy, latency, and operator burden in ways not fully quantified across studies.

established_findings.statement: Executable, emulation-grounded benchmarks that evaluate closed-loop behavior (not just generated commands) reveal failure modes beyond syntax or command errors and are necessary to assess operational reliability of LLM agents for NetOps.
limitations: Creating and maintaining high-fidelity executable benchmarks is resource intensive; existing benchmarks cover a subset of protocols/topologies.
Benchmark task design choices (hidden tests, task templates) influence which failure classes are exposed.

established_findings.statement: Confining LLMs to translation/translation-to-formal-model roles (i.e., using LLMs to build/verbalize formal models) and delegating long-horizon reasoning to verified solvers or formal engines reduces reliance on probabilistic model reasoning and improves verifiability.
limitations: Translation accuracy and up-to-dateness of the generated formal model depend on input artifacts and LLM translation quality.
Building and maintaining formal models at production scale remains engineering-heavy and may not be feasible for all operators.

established_findings.statement: Operator trust, human-in-the-loop oversight, and strong auditability (including concerns about operator-side audit independence) are central to deploying agentic NetOps; production-grade evidence for fully autonomous action without these assurances remains weak.
limitations: Human-factors findings rely on case studies and surveys; quantitative operator behavior under agentic NetOps deployments is still an emerging evidence stream.
The audit-independence argument addresses governance architecture rather than empirical failure rates.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what degree can LLM-driven automation safely enact network changes in live production without substantial guardrails, canaries, or external verification?
limitations: Available studies document principles, prototypes, and limited testbed/cluster experiments but do not establish broad production-case safety envelopes.
Operational heterogeneity (vendor devices, legacy protocols, partial observability) complicates generalization.

unresolved_questions.statement: How well do current synthetic or emulation-based benchmarks and repair datasets generalize to diverse production topologies, scale, and multi-vendor heterogeneity?
limitations: Benchmarks illustrate important failure classes but many remain limited in the diversity and provenance of ground-truth incidents.
Empirical transfer studies from benchmark to production are scarce.

unresolved_questions.statement: What are the most effective, operationally practical methods to provide calibrated, actionable uncertainty/confidence estimates for LLM outputs in NetOps workflows (so operators can decide when to trust/abstain)?
limitations: Uncertainty-quantification methods are active ML research; domain-specific calibration for structured configuration outputs and tool-calls remains under-explored.
Operational cost and latency of calibration techniques in closed-loop NetOps are not well characterized.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is a need for external, cryptographically anchored, independent audit trails and provenance mechanisms for agentic NetOps to avoid structural conflicts of interest inherent in operator-controlled audit records.
limitations: Architectural proposals exist, but deployment feasibility, integration cost, and standards adoption pathways require further study.
Cryptographic anchoring addresses audit independence but does not by itself prevent unsafe actions absent other controls.

candidate_gaps.statement: Public, large-scale, reproducible corpora of production-rooted misconfiguration and repair incidents (with verifiable ground truth) are scarce and would materially improve external validity of NetOps LLM evaluations.
limitations: Operational privacy, commercial sensitivity, and security concerns complicate creation and sharing of production incident corpora.
Synthetic generation pipelines partially mitigate scarcity but risk distributional mismatch to real incidents.

candidate_gaps.statement: Comparative evidence on multi-model generality (open vs closed models, model sizes) in closed-loop NetOps tasks is limited; systematic cross-model studies under identical executable-test harnesses are needed.
limitations: Existing evaluations often test a selection of models rather than exhaustive families; cost and API constraints affect comparability.
Differences in prompting, tool integration, and runtime harnesses confound simple attribution to model architecture alone.

excluded_claims: LLMs are production-ready to autonomously perform unrestricted NetOps changes without guardrails or formal verification.
A single LLM model (or model family) reliably replaces formal verification/solvers for network correctness at production scale.
Benchmarks presented to date prove that LLM-driven NetOps will generalize across all real-world topologies and vendor ecosystems.
